answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. Every claim climbs the fable of verified tasks, and a reviewer at the ivory re-runs the work instead of trusting the label. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the kernel of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
